10.text: An unfavorable indication of a shoulder-blade may be tested by divination

11.text: with the sinew of a reindeer-leg. A piece of sinew is wound tightly around

12.text: a splinter of wood several times. If it unwinds quite smoothly, this is

13.text: considered a favorable sign, and the indication of the shoulder-blade may be

14.text: rejected. If, on the contrary, it becomes entangled, this corroborates the

15.text: indication of the shoulder-blade, and some reverses are likely to happen. Then

16.text: another shoulder-blade may be tried for some other direction of moving.

17.text: The Maritime people use the shoulder-blades of the seal for purposes of

18.text: divination, but this is done less frequently, chiefly because there are no

19.text: questions to decide regarding the choice of direction of moving. The atten-

20.text: tion of the people is naturally directed, not so much to the possible result

21.text: of hunting-expeditions, as to procuring help and protection from the super-

22.text: natural forces, so as to obtain a favorable issue for the hunt.

23.text: The Chuvantzy and even the Lamut of the

24.text: Anadyr country have also adopted this way

25.text: of foretelling the future, and the latter probably

26.text: imitated it from their Chukchee neighbors.

27.text: The explanation of the lines, adopted by

28.text: the Lamut, is, however, simpler than that of

29.text: the Chukchee. The Lamut, for instance, do

30.text: not distinguish between the sea and the

31.text: mountain side of the shoulder-blade. They do

32.text: not even pay attention to the position in which

33.text: the blade is held, but are occupied exclusively

34.text: with the lines. Among the collections of the

35.text: Museum there are several shoulder-blades of

36.text: Lamut provenience, which were burnt over

37.text: the fire for divination. One of the most

38.text: characteristic is represented in Fig. 299. The

39.text: vertical line on it signifies the route of the

40.text: Lamut; one branch of the bifurcated line

41.text: coming from the left side signifies the com-

42.text: ing of the reindeer; and the body of the line signifies the joint way
